title: Cambodia Travel Guide 2026: 3, 5 & 7-Day Itineraries
description: Cambodia in 3, 5 or 7 days: Angkor Wat at sunrise, Bayon, Ta Prohm, Tonle Sap and Phnom Penh, with a US$ budget and visa tips for Indians.

sections.title: Why Visit Cambodia?
sections.html:
Cambodia is home to Angkor Wat, the world's largest religious monument, built as a Hindu temple to Vishnu. Its walls are carved with scenes from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the churning of the ocean of milk (Samudra Manthan), so Indian visitors often find it deeply moving.

Spend most of your time in Siem Reap for the Angkor temples and the Tonle Sap lake, then add the riverside capital, Phnom Penh. It's easy to pair with Thailand or Vietnam, and it's great value.

sections.title: Cambodia Itineraries: 3, 5 or 7 Days
sections.html: Pick 3, 5 or 7 days. Each longer plan builds on the shorter one: the first days stay the same and the extra days add more places. Costs are approximate per person per day; prices and timings change, so check before you book.

days.title: Siem Reap & Pub Street
periods: Morning
Arrive at Siem Reap Angkor International Airport (flights usually connect through Bangkok, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur or Ho Chi Minh City).
Afternoon
Buy your Angkor Pass at the official ticket centre (1, 3 or 7 days) and visit the Angkor National Museum.
Evening
Dinner and a stroll around Pub Street and the night markets.

days.title: Angkor Wat sunrise, Bayon & Ta Prohm
periods: Morning
Watch sunrise over Angkor Wat, then walk its galleries of Ramayana and Mahabharata carvings.
Afternoon
Explore Angkor Thom, the smiling stone faces of Bayon, and the tree-wrapped ruins of Ta Prohm.
Evening
Rest, then dinner in town. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the whole day.

days.title: Banteay Srei & the Grand Circuit
periods: Morning
Drive out to pink-sandstone Banteay Srei, the "temple of women", with the finest carvings at Angkor.
Afternoon
Visit Preah Khan and Neak Pean on the Grand Circuit.
Evening
Sunset at Pre Rup, then the Phare circus show.

days.title: Tonle Sap & on to Phnom Penh
periods: Morning
Boat trip to a stilt village on the Tonle Sap lake, such as Kampong Phluk.
Afternoon
Bus (about 5–6 hours) or fly to Phnom Penh.
Evening
Evening walk along the riverside Sisowath Quay.

days.title: Royal Palace & Phnom Penh
periods: Morning
Visit the Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda (cover shoulders and knees).
Afternoon
See the National Museum's Khmer sculptures, many of Hindu gods.
Evening
Sunset river cruise on the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers.

days.title: History & the Russian Market
periods: Morning
Visit Tuol Sleng (S-21) and the Choeung Ek memorial to learn about the Khmer Rouge years. It's sobering but important.
Afternoon
Shop at the Russian Market for silk, crafts and coffee.
Evening
Dinner at a Khmer restaurant or one of the city's Indian places.

days.title: Silk Island & departure
periods: Morning
Morning trip to Koh Dach (Silk Island) to see village silk weaving.
Afternoon
Last-minute shopping or a riverside lunch.
Evening
Fly home from Phnom Penh, usually connecting through a Southeast Asian hub.

sections.title: Food to Try in Cambodia
sections.html:
• Fish amok — Fish in a fragrant coconut and kroeung (lemongrass paste) curry, steamed in banana leaf; ask for tofu or vegetable amok.
  • Lok lak — Stir-fried beef with a lime and pepper dipping sauce.
  • Nom banh chok — Rice noodles with green fish curry, a classic Khmer breakfast.
  • Kuy teav — Noodle soup eaten for breakfast across the country.
  • Num pang — Cambodian baguette sandwiches, with tofu or vegetable versions easy to find.
  • Tropical fruit — Mango, rambutan and mangosteen from the markets.

For Indian travellers: Siem Reap and Phnom Penh have many Indian restaurants, and most Khmer kitchens can make vegetable or tofu versions of curries and stir-fries.

sections.title: Best Time to Visit Cambodia
sections.html:
Cool, dry season (November–February): the best time for Angkor, with sunny skies and lower humidity.

Hot season (March–May): very hot, often 35°C or more; start temples at sunrise and rest at midday.

Rainy season (June–October): green, quieter and cheaper, with short afternoon downpours. The Tonle Sap floating villages are at their best late in the season.

sections.title: Getting Around Cambodia
sections.html:
Flights from India: there are no direct flights at the time of writing. Connect through Bangkok, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur or Ho Chi Minh City to Siem Reap or Phnom Penh.

Around Angkor: hire a tuk-tuk and driver for the day (agree the route and price) or use the Grab and PassApp ride apps. E-bikes are a fun option for the small circuit.

Siem Reap–Phnom Penh: comfortable buses take about 5–6 hours; there are also short domestic flights.

Combining countries: buses run from Phnom Penh to Ho Chi Minh City and from Siem Reap to Bangkok.

sections.title: Travel Essentials
sections.html:
Entry for Indians: Indians need a visa. Get the tourist e-visa on the official portal (evisa.gov.kh) or a visa on arrival at the main airports and border crossings, usually about US$30 for 30 days. All air arrivals must also fill in the free Cambodia e-Arrival card online before the flight. Rules as of October 2026; always check the official website before you travel.

Money: US dollars are used everywhere alongside the Cambodian riel; you often get change in riel. Bring clean, untorn dollar notes. ATMs are common in cities.

Angkor Pass: buy only at the official ticket centre or online. Passes are around US$37 for 1 day, US$62 for 3 days and US$72 for 7 days; check current prices.

Daily budget (per person): a mid-range hotel share, food, a tuk-tuk and sightseeing come to about US$50–90 a day, plus the Angkor Pass.

SIM card: Smart, Cellcard and Metfone sell cheap tourist SIMs at the airport with your passport.

Plugs: types A, C and G, 230V. Many sockets take Indian two-pin plugs, but bring a universal adapter.

Etiquette and safety: cover shoulders and knees at temples and the Royal Palace, and don't touch monks or people's heads. Use licensed guides at Angkor, and never stray off marked paths in remote areas.
